clause_that_reaches_it: what a writer does outside Maugham is their risk; what Maugham does on their behalf is Maugham's
why_in_scope: This is a ROOT-only match, flagged as the protocol requires. The claim is contradicted — `UInt32(_:radix:)` accepts a leading `+`, so `#+12345` passes the validator — but no swatch inside Maugham can carry that form: the editor mints swatches only from `ColorPicker`/`NSColorSampler` through `hexString(from:)`, which formats uppercase `#RRGGBB`, and the MCP palette tools are read-only. The only producer is a hand-edited card file, which the clause's first half assigns to the writer. The clause's second half (what Maugham does on their behalf) is satisfied too: the leniently-accepted value is stored, rendered and re-parsed identically, so Maugham neither loses it nor misreports it — the swatch chip draws the colour the string actually denotes.
intent_expressed_when: not at all — no in-app control can express this input; it arrives only from an external edit

clause_that_reaches_it: words the writer AUTHORED are always recoverable; DERIVED material may be dropped but the drop must be reported
why_in_scope: The card body is authored prose (the editor labels the field "Notes… Anything else about this subject"). If the writer types a line that spells a known section name — `## Images`, `## Swatches`, `## Senses` — then on the next parse that line opens a section, and every non-`- ` line under it, up to the next heading, is discarded: the body comes back empty and the prose is gone from the file. The lost text is authored, not derived, so the clause's second half offers no licence; and nothing reports the loss to the writer either way. Scope is the model's own write-then-read of content Maugham itself stored, not an external hand-edit, so RULING-9 does not absolve it.
